title: “You’re tired… but you won’t admit it.”
paragraphs: “You’re tired… but you won’t admit it.”

Not physically.
Not just sleep.
Soul-tired.

The kind of exhaustion that no weekend can fix.
The kind that hides behind smiles, ministry, hustle, even prayers.
And then Jesus speaks.
“Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” — Gospel of Matthew 11:28
Come.

Not perform.
Not pretend.
Not prove.
Come.

You’ve been carrying things God never asked you to carry.
Shame from yesterday.
Fear of tomorrow.
Pressure to be “okay” when you’re not.
Heavy.
But here’s what we miss…

Jesus didn’t say, “Fix yourself, then come.”
He didn’t say, “Clean up, then I’ll accept you.”
He said—come as you are.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because the cross was never for the strong.
It was for the collapsing.
The burnt out.
The secretly breaking.

Sin made the weight.
But Jesus carried it.
All of it.

At Calvary, your burden met His body.
Your chaos met His mercy.
Your exhaustion met His finished work.
This is not just rest from problems.
This is rest for your soul.

Deep.
Holy.
Unshakeable.
The kind only Christ can give.
So stop running.
Come home.
Right now. Not when you feel ready.
Just come.
